title: Equity investments portfolio — Crestview Industries
instructions: Crestview Industries holds several equity investments at December 31, Year 1. Determine the accounting model for each and compute the equity-method amounts for its investment in Delmar Co.

exhibits.title: Investment summary
exhibits.content:
| Investee | Ownership | Facts |
|---|---:|---|
| Alpine Corp. | 3% | Listed on NYSE; no board seat |
| Delmar Co. | 25% | Two of eight board seats; purchased Jan 1, Year 1 |
| Everly Inc. | 12% | Private; no observable prices; Crestview supplies 70% of Everly's inventory and has a board seat |
| Fenwick LLC | 65% | Crestview appoints the majority of managers |
| Glenco Ltd. | 6% | Private; no readily determinable fair value; no influence |

exhibits.title: Delmar Co. acquisition data
exhibits.content:
- Crestview paid **$2,500,000** for 25% of Delmar on January 1, Year 1.
- Delmar's book value on that date was **$8,000,000**.
- Delmar's inventory was undervalued by **$400,000** (all sold during Year 1).
- Delmar's patent was undervalued by **$1,200,000**; remaining life **8 years**.
- Any remaining excess is goodwill.
- Delmar's Year 1 net income: **$1,600,000**; dividends paid: **$500,000**.

parts.prompt: Select the accounting model for each investment.

rows.label: Alpine Corp.
rows.explanation: No influence and a readily determinable fair value.

rows.label: Everly Inc.
rows.explanation: Below 20%, but a board seat and material supply relationship indicate significant influence.

rows.label: Glenco Ltd.
rows.explanation: No influence and no readily determinable fair value → may elect the measurement alternative.

rows.label: Excess of cost over Crestview's share of book value
